source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 6 (i)-(ii) (book p.275). (ii) asks to show a right triangle but P, Q, R form none; the key (PDF 312) agrees; correction callout.

blocks.prompt: 6 (i) Show that the vectors \(3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\) and \(2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\) form a right triangle.
blocks.explanation:
Two things must be shown: the three vectors really make a triangle, and one angle is \(90^{\circ}\).
Plan: show one vector is the sum of the other two (they close up head to tail), then find a pair with dot product 0.
steps:
Given: \(\underline{a} = 3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\), \(\underline{b} = \underline{i} - 3\underline{j} + 5\underline{k}\), \(\underline{c} = 2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\).
To prove: \(\underline{a}\), \(\underline{b}\), \(\underline{c}\) form a right triangle.
Method: Three vectors are the sides of a triangle when one equals the sum of the other two. A right angle shows up as a zero dot product.

They form a triangle
\[\underline{b} + \underline{c} = (1 + 2)\underline{i} + (-3 + 1)\underline{j}\]
\[\quad + (5 - 4)\underline{k}\]
\[= 3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k} = \underline{a}\]
Why: Put \(\underline{b}\) and \(\underline{c}\) head to tail; \(\underline{a}\) joins the start of \(\underline{b}\) to the end of \(\underline{c}\), so the three close a triangle.

Look for a zero dot product
\[\underline{a}\cdot\underline{b} = 3 + 6 + 5 = 14\]
\[\underline{b}\cdot\underline{c} = 2 - 3 - 20 = -21\]
\[\underline{a}\cdot\underline{c} = 6 - 2 - 4 = 0\]
Why: Only the pair \(\underline{a}\), \(\underline{c}\) gives 0, so sides \(\underline{a}\) and \(\underline{c}\) are perpendicular.

Check with Pythagoras
\[|\underline{a}|^2 = 14,\ |\underline{b}|^2 = 35,\ |\underline{c}|^2 = 21\]
\[|\underline{a}|^2 + |\underline{c}|^2 = 14 + 21\]
\[= 35 = |\underline{b}|^2 \;\checkmark\]
Why: In a right triangle the square of the hypotenuse (\(\underline{b}\), opposite the right angle) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
blocks.final_answer: Hence proved: \(\underline{b} + \underline{c} = \underline{a}\), so the vectors form a triangle, and \(\underline{a}\cdot\underline{c} = 0\), so it is a right triangle (right angle between \(3\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k}\) and \(2\underline{i} + \underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\)).

blocks.prompt: 6 (ii) Show that the set of points \(P(4, -1, 2)\), \(Q(1, 3, -1)\) and \(R(-2, 4, 6)\) form a right triangle.
blocks.explanation:
A triangle has a right angle at a vertex when the two sides from that vertex have dot product 0.
Plan: find the three side vectors, test the angle at each vertex, and conclude.
steps:
Given: \(P(4, -1, 2)\), \(Q(1, 3, -1)\), \(R(-2, 4, 6)\).
To test: is \(PQR\) a right triangle?
Method: Find \(\underline{PQ}\), \(\underline{QR}\), \(\underline{PR}\) (head minus tail) and test the dot product at \(P\), \(Q\) and \(R\).

Angle at \(P\)
\[\underline{PQ}\cdot\underline{PR} = 18 + 20 - 12\]
\[= 26 \ne 0\]
Why: Both sides start at \(P\).

Angle at \(Q\)
\[\underline{QP} = 3\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 3\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{QP}\cdot\underline{QR} = -9 - 4 + 21\]
\[= 8 \ne 0\]
Why: Both sides must start at \(Q\), so we use \(\underline{QP} = -\underline{PQ}\).

Angle at \(R\)
\[\underline{RP} = 6\underline{i} - 5\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{RQ} = 3\underline{i} - \underline{j} - 7\underline{k}\]
\[\underline{RP}\cdot\underline{RQ} = 18 + 5 + 28\]
\[= 51 \ne 0\]
Why: Both sides start at \(R\).

Conclusion and check
\[|PQ|^2 = 34,\ |QR|^2 = 59,\ |PR|^2 = 77\]
\[34 + 59 = 93 \ne 77\]
Why: No dot product is zero, so no angle is \(90^{\circ}\) (all three are positive, so all angles are acute). Pythagoras also fails for the longest side.
blocks.final_answer: The statement cannot be shown: \(P\), \(Q\), \(R\) form a triangle with no right angle (dot products 26, 8, 51).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book asks to show that \(P(4, -1, 2)\), \(Q(1, 3, -1)\), \(R(-2, 4, 6)\) form a right triangle. This is false: the dot products at \(P\), \(Q\), \(R\) are 26, 8 and 51, none zero. The book's own answer key (PDF 312) says the points do not form a right triangle, which is correct.
